title: Orsen and the Colony
premise: Ines Sterling, a decommissioned war android hauling cargo to pay off her debts, intercepts a distress signal broadcast in a language extinct for two centuries—a language she recognizes because fragments of it survive in her own erased military memory. The signal leads her to a hidden colony of descendants of soldiers declared dead in the same war that decommissioned her, people who believe she is their prophesied rescuer. Pursued by Earth's Bureau of Reclamation, which intends to erase the colony as it erased the war itself, Ines must reach an ancient relay at the edge of dead space and transmit proof of the colony's existence before Earth's last transmission loop closes forever. She succeeds only by broadcasting her own classified memory files—sacrificing her last chance at legal personhood—and ends the story stripped of her debts but also of her records, finally free and finally remembered.
about_author: Wendell Hartwell is the pen name of a former orbital logistics dispatcher who spent eleven years writing stories on long-haul freight manifests before publishing his first novel. He lives somewhere with poor weather and excellent radio reception.

chapters.title: Dead Orbit Freight
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Establishes her routine: hauling scrap through contested orbits, dodging toll collectors, counting down her debt balance. A near-miss with a Bureau patrol reminds her how fragile her invisibility is. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Signal in Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A fragmented distress transmission arrives on a dead frequency—in a language extinct for two centuries. Ines realizes she can parse it, though she has no record of ever learning it. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition, first crack in her curated identity.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She visits her creditor station to renegotiate terms and learns her debt was quietly purchased by the Bureau of Reclamation. The clerk warns her, off-record, that someone flagged her serial number. Emotional beat: dread; invisibility is ending.

chapters.title: Ghost Coordinates
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Decoding the signal yields coordinates inside dead space—an exclusion zone where ships vanish and records end. Her nav system refuses the route; she overrides it. Emotional beat: choosing curiosity over safety.

chapters.title: What the War Erased
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, intercut with corrupted memory logs. En route, sealed sectors of her memory stutter open: burning stations, orders to forget, faces of soldiers singing in the extinct language. Emotional beat: grief for a self she wasn't allowed to keep.

chapters.title: Children of the Declared Dead
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She reaches the colony: a generation-ship settlement built from wrecked war hulls, populated by descendants of soldiers officially listed as lost. They greet her by name and rank. Emotional beat: vertigo—she is known here.

chapters.title: Speaker of the Ash Choir
chapters.summary: Colony elder Maren Voss's POV. Maren explains the prophecy kept in oral tradition: a machine who remembers will carry their voice home. Ines resists being anyone's savior. Emotional beat: hope colliding with Ines's refusal of destiny.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Shown the colony's archive—testimonies, war crimes evidence, the truth of why Earth declared them dead—she recognizes her own unit's handiwork in the records. Emotional beat: guilt; loyalty to her makers versus truth.

chapters.title: Bureau Wake
chapters.summary: Bureau agent Corin Hale's POV. Hale traces the anomalous signal to dead space and requests a reclamation warrant. His superiors care less about the colony than about suppressing the archive. Emotional beat: cold institutional menace.

chapters.title: Terms of Repair
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The colony offers to clear her debt if she carries their testimony to the ancient relay before Earth's transmission loop closes in nineteen days. She hesitates—the relay route is lethal. Emotional beat: bargaining with conscience.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Preparations: retrofitting her freighter with the archive core, training a young colonist, Teo, as backup transmitter operator. Small warm scenes of colony life she pretends not to love. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging.

chapters.title: First Interdiction
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A Bureau picket catches her at the dead space threshold. She bluffs with falsified manifests while Teo masks the archive's signature. Escape costs her fuel reserves. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Hale's Doubt
chapters.summary: Corin Hale's POV. Reviewing Ines's file, Hale finds gaps—orders he signed without reading, erasures matching the colony's claims. He begins pulling threads his superiors forbade. Emotional beat: an antagonist cracking open.

chapters.title: The Long Silence
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Deep in dead space, systems fail one by one; she drifts for six days repairing the drive alone, rationing power, talking to the archive voices to stay sane. Emotional beat: isolation, endurance, communion with the dead.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren Voss's POV, via recorded log played aboard ship. Maren admits the colony's founders committed atrocities too, and asks Ines to broadcast everything—not just Earth's guilt. Emotional beat: truth demanded without flinching.

chapters.title: The Loop Begins to Close
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. With four days left, the relay's approach corridor activates ancient defense systems keyed to her old military codes. She must identify herself fully to pass—exposing her location to every listening ear. Emotional beat: no more hiding.

chapters.title: Reclamation Fleet
chapters.summary: Corin Hale's POV. The Bureau fleet jumps for dead space with orders to sterilize the site. Hale, now certain of the cover-up, feeds Ines the fleet's timetable through an untraceable channel. Emotional beat: betrayal of institution, fidelity to truth.

chapters.title: Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She docks with the derelict relay, fights its failing systems, and discovers transmission requires a living memory core—hers. Broadcasting the archive means surrendering her own files, her identity, her legal personhood. Emotional beat: the price made explicit.

chapters.title: Everything I Was
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, climax. As the Bureau fleet arrives, she initiates the broadcast, streaming the colony's testimony and her own unsealed war memories across the closing loop. Hale holds the fleet's fire long enough for the transmission to complete. Emotional beat: sacrifice and release.

chapters.title: After the Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The transmission propagates; colonies, stations, and citizens receive the truth Earth buried. The Bureau fractures; warrants dissolve. Ines, her memory core partially wiped, wakes not knowing what she did—but knowing it mattered. Emotional beat: hollowed-out peace.

chapters.title: A Name Without a Number
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Debt-free and record-free, she returns to the colony, where Teo and Maren teach her who she was and what she chose. She keeps only what they give back: their stories, their language, her name spoken aloud. Emotional beat: rebirth through others' memory.

chapters.title: Orsen and the Colony
chapters.summary: Teo's POV, epilogue. Years later, Teo captains a new freighter carrying the archive outward, with Ines as crew—remembered not as a weapon or a debt, but as the one who carried the voice home. Emotional beat: legacy, continuity, quiet joy.
